_what: The whole-generated render fielded in the walk-off (walkoff.html BODY B slot, screen right). The reproducible INPUT; the sheets it produces are build output under assets/original/cipher_render/.
_decided: 2026-08-02 - staged for audition, not canon. Re-pointed the same day from 'CIPHER (canon test)' (d8632f4a, 68x68, a pre-lock cousin with its own face) to the LOCKED D1 appearance (pixellab_cipher.json), so the hybrid and the render wear the same identity and the audition's only variable is pack animation vs whole generation.
_finding: The template skeleton holds the walk the v3 prompts could not: contralateral arm/leg phase is correct on every generated facing, because the phase comes from the rig, not from the prompt. Verified frame-by-frame 2026-08-02 on the canon-test cousin first (east view is the legible one). The dead_ends note in pixellab_cipher.json ('template re-poses and repaints; destroys the face and visor') is the caveat this staging exists to judge by eye, now on the locked character itself.
_caveat: The room's left/right facings map to PixelLab's south-west/south-east, not west/east: the pack's side sheets are 3/4 views, and a true-profile render standing next to them would be auditioning a different dialect, not a different body. The west/east template walks exist in the same animation group but are not molded into sheets.
idle_from: breathing-idle template frames (4/facing). The rotation stills are no longer molded as idle — they remain the GROUND-ROW measurement source, because the anchor is the standing row and the breath bobs.
idle_animation_type: breathing-idle (template) for south/south-west/south-east; north is v3 custom pinned to the north rotation still
_idle_north_dead_end: The template breathing-idle painted the full visor band on the BACK of the head in 3 of 4 north frames (frame 2 was correct; the north WALK was correct, so the template does not force a face). A same-template re-roll is blocked by dedup; delete-and-regenerate would re-roll the three good facings. Fix: v3 with custom_start_frame pinned to the north rotation and a state-shaped prompt ('hair only in every frame') - the 'ask for a state, not a motion' finding, third confirmation. Measured: 0 visor-cyan head pixels in all 4 v3 frames vs 8 in each bad template frame.

run._what: RUN for the whole-generated body - the first verb landed after the slice verdict (2026-08-09), template-first per doctrine. Rides the root character/cdn_base; three facings kept from the template, north from the ladder below.
_ladder: running-8-frames template, 4 dirs at ai_freedom=0: south/south-west/south-east WON at 1 gen/dir. north FAILED - 6 of 8 frames rendered the whole BODY frontal (visor and vest toward camera on a figure running away); frames 1 and 5 were honest backs. The walk's north was correct in its day, so the template does not force a face - it rolled one. 4 generations, 3 facings kept.

v3 pinned to the north ROTATION still with a state-shaped prompt (the idle-north repair, replayed): FAILED twice over - a STANDING reference anchors standing (about 1px of motion across 8 frames, the same anchoring the kneel ladder measured) and identity drifted (helmet lost to bare hair). 1 generation, deleted from the provider; this entry is the record.

v3 pinned to template north frame 1 - a good MID-STRIDE back frame from the same verb's own group: WON at 1 generation. 8 frames, real cycle motion (100-280px changing per frame), helmet and jacket held, 0 visor-cyan pixels in every frame.
run._doctrine: For a single bad direction of a CYCLIC verb, pin v3 to a good mid-cycle frame of the same verb from the sibling group - never to the rotation still. The reference anchors pose family, facing and identity TOGETHER: a standing still anchors standing. Sixth confirmation that looking at pixels beats the aggregate metric - the first repair scored 0 on the visor metric and was a standing sway wearing a run's name.
run.animation_type: running-8-frames (template) for south/south-west/south-east; north is v3 pinned to template north frame 1 (group 2d18c95b-c3bb-488e-8eae-17285437c701)

dash._what: DASH for the whole-generated body - the sixth verb (2026-08-09), and the first ONE-SHOT: the room's locked verb that MOVES (L key, DASH_SPEED burst over the sheet's frames). The first verb generated by COMPOSING the paid-for doctrines: a lunge STATE anchors the pose family, then v3 animates from the state's own rotations - keep_first_frame makes the state still the launch frame, the same job the pack's frame 1 does.
_ladder: create_character_state (lunge launch pose, palette snap): south/south-west/south-east WON - deep forward lean, heights 28-31 vs standing 32. north STOOD UP AGAIN (fourth back-view pose refusal: kneel state, idle template, run template, now dash state) - legs strode but the torso stayed bolt upright at full height, feet 3 rows through the floor. 20 generations.

v3 six-plus-reference frames on the state's own rotations, 3 dirs at once: south-west and south-east WON at 1 gen each - real burst motion, 328-431 px changing per frame (more violent than run's 100-280, right for a burst), identity held. south FAILED on identity: the model peeled the visor OFF the face and painted it as a floating cyan speed streak - the palette's one saturated color became the motion effect. 3 generations, 2 kept.

south v2 with the invariant named per frame ('visor fixed on the face in every frame, no light trails or motion streaks'): WON at 1 generation - the guard-clause prompt shape's third save (idle north 'hair only', now this). The dead south dir (cf7ffb89, group 3da81bbc) stays in the provider as provenance; its group also holds the good SW/SE, so it cannot be deleted without re-rolling winners.

north: ROW SURGERY on the state's north still (whole figure up 3 - feet back to the standing line - then head block rows 13-26 dropped 4: the pack's own away-dash lean, head swallowed into the shoulders), then v3 pinned to the surgered anchor via custom_start_frame: WON at 1 generation. 0 visor-cyan in all 7 frames, the lean holds, real stride at 261-300 px per frame. kneel's scalpel makes the anchor; run's pin doctrine rides it.
dash._doctrine: One-shot verbs COMPOSE the doctrines rather than needing a new one: STATE-first anchors the key pose, v3 rides the state's own rotations, and keep_first_frame ships the state still as the launch frame. The back view's repair is surgery-then-pin. And the guard clause - name the invariant, per frame, in the prompt - is now three-for-three on facings the free roll broke.
dash._dialect: left/right ship from south-west/south-east (3/4), matching facing_map. 7 frames at the room's 14fps = the composed dialect's 500ms one-shot exactly. NO authored streak: the pack's launch streak is one frame at 71ms, and the render's burst carries 260-430 px of change per frame plus the room's actual position burst - the read does not need it. A palette-white streak stays available as a polish pass if the designer wants one after walking it.
dash._not_standing: dash is a LUNGE: sources dip and lean like run's gait. It joins no standing-row envelope and the re-frame's standing anchor guard does not apply to it.

_north_surgery._why: PROVENANCE, not an executable spec - unlike kneel's north_surgery, which walkoff_render_sheets.py consumes, nothing reads these numbers at build time: the shipped north frames come pre-surgered from dash_animation_dirs.north on the state's CDN. Recorded so the anchor's construction is reproducible. The state's north kept the head at standing height with a leg through the floor - the inverse of the pack's away-dash geometry (head drops, feet stay). The surgered still is frame 0 of the shipped north strip AND the v3 anchor that kept the other six frames in the lean's pose family.

aim._what: AIM for the whole-generated body - the second held-pose verb (state-first per doctrine, decided 2026-08-09) and the first ARMED one. The sidearm ships IN the body's pixels, part of the character's kit like the jacket; the rig's socket export (sockets_aim_{facing}.json, the aim pose PR) is the muzzle DECLARATION consumers read - FIRE's bloom placement and acceptance checks - per doc D2: a socket makes the weapon a declaration, not an inference.
_ladder: create_character_state with a state-shaped, per-joint prompt ('standing and aiming a compact pistol: right arm extended straight forward at shoulder level, arm horizontal, holding a small dark energy pistol with a cyan glow strip, left arm relaxed hanging at the side, legs in a normal standing stance'), palette snap on: WON at ONE state, zero repairs, 20 generations. All four roster facings passed on sight and on measurement: identity held (helmet, visor, jacket), body rows match idle ROW FOR ROW per facing (heights 32/31/32/32, same ground rows), chirality is right-handed and 3D-consistent across every rotation - the dialect upgrade the composed mirror cheat could never afford.
aim._doctrine: Held-pose verbs go STATE-first - second confirmation, and the cleanest: one state, no ladder rungs burned. The prompt speaks the rig guide's sentences as anatomy (arm level, shoulder height, off arm hanging), not as a motion.
aim._dialect: left/right ship from south-west/south-east (3/4), matching facing_map. The pose is the licensed thug pack's gunplay law, cited by roster_mold's own synthesis notes: 'the arm is the pose, the flash is the verb.' It is NOT the composed roster's chest grip - compose lifted HEAL's draw because it cannot repose a limb; the rig can, so the render body aims like the reference. Hard facings per the same law: head-on the weapon is an aperture glint at the chest (measured: cyan at (28,30), viewer-left = the RIGHT hand); facing away, only the raised hand and tip break the silhouette beside the head, no weapon shown.
aim._guide: rig pose + sockets: scripts/roto_mannequin.py ROTO_POSE=aim. Compass note for anyone comparing guides to provider stills: the rig's SW render shows the figure facing what PixelLab calls south-east, and vice versa - the rig azimuth orbits the opposite way on the east-west axis. The sockets sidecar is side-agnostic by contract; the aim arm is the rig's arm_L, which is the figure's anatomical RIGHT.

breath._why: held stance, the kneel's breath dialect at the same amplitude: frame 2 shifts the upper 40% of body rows down one pixel - compression. The shifted band's floor (~row 28 at 64px) sits ABOVE the roster facings' weapon line (south-west/south-east arm rows 30+, south's chest glint at 30), so the barrel never shears across the boundary; the north glint rides the shifted head as one piece. A molder change that moves this boundary must re-check that fact.

fire._what: FIRE for the whole-generated body - the seventh verb (2026-08-09), the second one-shot, and the first verb that buys NO state: it rides the Aim state's own rotations (keep_first_frame ships the aim still as frame 0), so the shot begins and ends in the stance that hosts it and the room's resume-into-held-aim seam is pixel-exact by construction. Five frames at the room's 10fps = the composed dialect's 500ms shot; the room's FIRE_SPILL [0, 3.4, 2.2, 1.1, 0] indexes these same frames, so the shipped strips must decay.
_ladder: v3 four-plus-reference on the Aim state's rotations, all four roster dirs at once, visor guard clause in the prompt from the start: north WON at 1 gen - the glint builds beside the raised hand, exactly where the away-facing dialect puts it. south told the wrong story (a chest orb growing into a torso-swallowing starburst - taking a hit, not firing one); south-west dropped the arm on f1 and FLIPPED the figure on f3-f4, flash on the wrong side; south-east's f2 was the ladder's best fire frame but f3 stretched the flash into a beam back across the head (the dash speed-streak failure at a new address). 4 generations, 1 kept.

south v2, position named ('at the pistol aperture, never larger than the head'): the flash migrated UP instead - a four-pointed star square on the face, visor swallowed for two frames. 1 generation, dead; group 0b3bb7b9 is the provenance.

south-west v2 + south-east v2, invariants named per frame (arm level, never flips / flash at the muzzle tip only, no beams): south-east WON at 1 gen - hold, burst with a real recoil swing, muzzle-side fade, settle. south-west held facing and arm this time but the flash never died (bloom 9/15/29/29 across f1-f4). Found on the way in: v3 dedup fingerprints the prompt's OPENING ~30 chars (the truncated type string) - a re-roll that keeps its first words comes back 'already queued'; reword the opening, not just the guards. 2 generations, 1 kept as generated, 1 kept by surgery.

south v3, position named NEGATIVELY ('below the face, never touches the visor') plus timing ('bursts on the first moving frame'): WON at 1 gen on position and story - chest burst, face clear, wisp settle. The peak still landed on f2: the anticipation-then-burst prior held in all seven rolls. 1 generation. 8 total for the verb.
fire._doctrine: The scalpel cuts TIME the way it cuts rows. The model's animation prior puts the burst on f2 (anticipation first - seven of seven rolls), while the room's spill curve decays from f1, so the record declares stage_frames per facing and the molder ships the source frames in that order. Anticipation and recovery are visually symmetric at one frame each: south-west's decay is its own frames walked backward. No rung was burned re-rolling against a prior that surgery composes away.
fire._dialect: left/right ship from south-west/south-east (3/4), matching facing_map. Bloom strictly decays across shipped f1-f3 and the strip is dark on f0/f4 - the exact frames FIRE_SPILL lights. down/up die faster than the laterals (shipped f3 dark): the 1.1 spill step briefly outlives the drawn bloom there, the same magnitude as the composed sheet's own 4-pixel spent ring. The flash reads white-hot core on the laterals and cyan on down/up - the palette's own highlight ramp, judged at 1x.

stage_frames._why: shipped strip = source frames in this order, EXECUTED by the molder (unlike dash's provenance-only surgery note). Every facing ends on source frame 0 because the lock releases into a held aim on the very next update: a settle that only NEARLY matches the stance pops at 10fps (up first shipped its source settle, 71px off the still - review bot measured the pop; both ends of the seam are pixel-checked now). left is its own frames walked backward - that roll never let the flash die, and reversed, its wind-up nudge reads as the recoil coming home.

muzzle._space: 64-canvas pixels: the rig's sockets_aim_{rig_facing}.json hand_L point (the anatomical RIGHT hand, anchored 96x80 sheet space, authoring run 2026-08-09 on bpy 5.2.0) minus the render_canvas96 offset (dx 15, dy 10). Rig facings mirror PixelLab's on the east-west axis (see the aim block's _guide): left reads rig SE, right reads rig SW. dir is the forearm unit vector, elbow toward hand - the muzzle line, doc D2's declaration made consumable.
muzzle._why: mode side consumes the FULL forearm vector: bloom must sit along the muzzle line from margin behind the hand to reach ahead of it, within perp of the line (keepers measured along +3.8..+18.4 and perp <= 9.3; the flip dies at along -27.6, the beam at perp 16.8 - the first cut compared x alone and a review bot caught that it consumed neither bound). mode radius holds the head-on/away flash to the aperture (the face-star and the orb-burst die here). r covers the barrel past the wrist (~4px - the socket is the HAND, per doc D2 the fore_* origin fact) plus the burst's own tips (~7px).

bloom._why: bloom = pixels with blue >= 200 outside the 2px-dilated baseline of shipped frame 0. The blue floor keeps skin and jacket highlights out of the metric; the dilation absorbs authored kit (visor, glow strip) riding the recoil - measured at 2px on south-east's settle, not assumed. These numbers were EXECUTED before they were recorded: all four keepers pass and all four dead rolls are rejected (the growers on decay, the star/orb/flip/beam on containment).

kneel._what: KNEEL for the whole-generated body - the first verb built with no pack pixels, and the first verb the roto rig choreographed (PR #97's kneel guide named the pose; the prompt spoke it as per-frame properties). Decided 2026-08-08, designer judging stills against the rig guide.
_ladder: v3 state-shaped prompt on the Idle rotation: FAILED. 1px of body-height drop measured against the rig's predicted ~5px (84% of standing). A v3 reference still anchors POSE as strongly as identity - the two are inseparable. 1 generation.

create_character_state('kneeling on one knee'): WON. Re-posing is that tool's whole job; identity held via group + palette snap. south/west/east/south-west/south-east all read as kneels; north barely folded (106% of standing). ~20 generations.

inpaint of the north lower body: FAILED twice over. The mask froze the head a kneel needs to drop, and the Gemini tier painted palette-foreign red pixels into a smeared fold at 64px. ~20 generations, discarded.
row surgery on the state's north (kneel_frames algorithm, d=5, jacket pools 1px/side for 2 rows): WON at zero generations. The back view is the one facing where 'reads as a shorter man' IS the pose.
kneel._doctrine: Held-pose verbs go STATE-first; cyclic verbs go template-first; a v3 prompt alone moves a pose about one pixel; the back view belongs to row surgery. Fifth confirmation that looking at pixels beats the aggregate metric: the 84%-height check flunked poses that read correctly, because it encoded the RIG's forward torso lean and the model chose an upright-torso kneel.
kneel._dialect: left/right ship from south-west/south-east (3/4), NOT west/east (true profile), matching facing_map above and the pack's side-view dialect. The profiles read equally well and remain on the state's rotations as provenance.

north_surgery._why: the state's north kept the head at 106% of standing; kneel_frames row surgery drops the torso and lets the legs absorb it, and the jacket pools a pixel a side to sell the fold - the pack's own north kneel was made exactly this way

breath._why: the pack KNEEL is a 2-frame held pose; frame 2 shifts the upper 40% of body rows down one pixel - compression, the same breath dialect at the same amplitude
